description: The bar chart presents average performance values across five training methods evaluated on 11 datasets. The horizontal axis contains the method categories labeled, from left to right, “Standard,” “Self-RAG,” “FactTune,” “ClInGS (w/),” and “ClInGS,” and the vertical axis is a numeric scale labeled “Average Performance” on a linear scale with tick marks at regular 10-unit intervals, spanning from 0 up to about 60 (with the tallest bar extending slightly above the 60 gridline). Each method is represented by a single solid-colored bar: “Standard” is orange at approximately 52, “Self-RAG” is a light khaki/olive color at approximately 54, “FactTune” is light green at approximately 51–52, “ClInGS (w/)” is medium blue at approximately 54, and “ClInGS” is dark blue at approximately 59–60. The bars are not stacked or grouped beyond being placed side-by-side, there is no legend shown, and no individual bars appear specially annotated or outlined; the category order visually places lower bars earlier and higher bars later, with “ClInGS” appearing as the tallest bar and “FactTune” as the shortest.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the average performance across five training methods on 11 datasets. The horizontal axis lists the methods: 'Standard,' 'Self-RAG,' 'FactTune,' 'ClInGS (w/),' and 'ClInGS,' in ascending order of performance. The vertical axis represents 'Average Performance,' ranging from 0 to 60, with intervals of 10 units. The 'ClInGS' method consistently outperformed all others, achieving an average performance of approximately 62, while 'FactTune' showed the lowest performance at around 48. The 'Self-RAG' method demonstrated a slight decline compared to 'Standard,' which maintained stable performance across datasets. The chart highlights the superiority of the 'ClInGS' methods, particularly the standalone 'ClInGS' approach, which exhibited a significant improvement over its variant 'ClInGS (w/).'
